# A sales pipeline shows the value of deals in each stage

## Context

The ninth Task Board example in the planning family slate answers a sales team's question: how much business sits in each stage, and what changes when one deal advances? Its prerequisite is #21868. The slate steward confirmed the frame and publication route on 22 November.

## The Problem

The current eight board examples cover task workflows, swimlanes, scale, WIP limits, card designs, editing, selection and column arrangement. The Columns example uses studio commissions but demonstrates arranging the stages. A visitor still has no example where the value of each deal explains the stage total.

## The Architectural Reality

`Neo.board.Container` binds to a store of model records. Its normal card drag and `moveCard` write status to that store. The optional column total is in #21868. The reusable card items display text and people. The five themes and startup resolver are demonstrated by `examples/board/columns`.

## The Fix

Build `examples/board/salesPipeline` with a small set of fixed, fictional deals that fit on the first desktop screen. Show the formatted value and owner on each card. Four named sales stages show dollar totals immediately. A single on-screen instruction identifies a specific proposal to move into negotiation. Drag or use an accessible action to advance that deal. Reset restores the opening state. Use the same records for every value and the normal board writer for both routes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The visitor sees each stage's dollar total and individual deal values and owners on the first frame. At 1440 × 900 the named proposal and destination are visible together. At 390 × 844 the named action and reachable stages work without page-wide overflow.
- [ ] Advancing the named proposal subtracts its amount from Proposal and adds it to Negotiation. An ordinary pointer drag moves a deal through the same board. Reset restores the opening state. Verify in-browser on real records, in every configured theme, and retain the desktop and phone Neo Dark first frames for the steward.
- [ ] The example has a usable catalog record (`board-sales-pipeline`), a linked opening-frame cover on Pages, and no new capture steps, selectors or per-example viewport manifest. Register the record through the authoring path settled by #21539. Until then the PR body carries the record. The release steward owns the final catalog look.

## Out of Scope

Remote CRM integration, probability-weighted forecasts and persistence are independent product questions.
